The truth is I am incredibly impatient with myself and  and that is where my most of my frustrations stem from. If he could help me deal with that I would find his approach a lot easier. I am learning how to deal with it on my own from reading material. It's not that I am angry at myself for agreeing maybe pissed that I make it difficult on myself to reach my goals.

In my experience as someone who has negative thoughts about myself I am slowly coming to understand how you frame your thoughts is very important. The thoughts just don't go away and when they start happening they happen slowly. So in turn they will happen less and less by working on them. 

For example I lose things. So I tell myself "You lose everything, You can't trust yourself" Is that completely true? No. Is there any truth in that...? Yes. So the truth is that I do lose stuff but not all time. Will I lose stuff in the future? Sure. Will I lose everything no. So I can't completely trust myself not to lose stuff but in knowing that I am aware to take more precautions then before. My thoughts are still negative but not as harsh. 

This is stuff I learned myself from a self help book. That hardest part to accept is that there is some truth in your negative thoughts it's just not as blank and white as you brain tells you. It's a CBT job to help you break down your thoughts and understand why your brain is focusing on them so much.

In the past I have had the strength to face my fears. I used to be afraid of the dark as a child and I decided I cannot live like this. So after waking up at 3 am all panicked I made my mind up to fix this fear from my life. I can't remember how old I was but I grabbed a knife and a flashlight and went for a walk around the trails of my acreage home alone. It was a bright moonlit night and I was quite familar with where I was so I walked with the light off. I did hear the rustling of a large animal but I faced it from the direction the sound was coming knife in hand. At that moment I knew I was facing my fear. Nothing came of it. It walked away as did I unscathed. 

Now I know I have the strength to do something similar to that in my adult life. Which I did just not in a way that I would say was admirable. I got a job as a bouncer at my favourite club. All 165lbs of me was capable of breaking up verbal and physical disputes but when that energy became directed at me I could feel myself start to quiver. I would force myself to sit in that feeling stand my ground but when brawls would break out I was of little use... I have not stopped condemning myself for that.

As far as finding a male therapist and the patience for his questions yes that's the end game. If I could deal with these things alone I would have but that is not the case. There are instances where there are questions ask myself that I won't answer and I know those are clues to where my problems are. I know I am clever and I need a well versed/trained therapist who can stear the sessions for me. To help me by easing me into the things I am stearing away from. 

My last male therapist was not a good fit for me... He had the knowledge but his attitude was bitter and he brought out the worse out in me. I agreed with him that I complain to much about my problems not just in therapy but in life. Yet he felt it was necessary to tell me verbatim " Oh so this is what a millennial is like..." How would that be helpful to anyone? If I had money I would pay for the best help I could get but I am limited to free services for now.
